name: nft_pipapo_avx2_lookup_8b_4
prose: Static function nft_pipapo_avx2_lookup_8b_4(map, fill, f, offset, pkt, first, last), an AVX2 lookup step for one field of an nft pipapo set; the caller must be inside a kernel FPU section with ymm15 zero. It scans each 256-bit block i of the bitmaps from offset up to f->bsize / NFT_PIPAPO_LONGS_PER_M256. For each block it ANDs the four buckets selected by pkt[0] .. pkt[3] (each one of 256 buckets). When first is false and the map block is all zero the block is skipped and left unchanged; if the combined bucket result (ANDed with the map block when first is false) is zero it stores zero into the map block (via ymm15). Otherwise it stores that result into the map block and calls nft_pipapo_avx2_refill on it: with last false that call fills the fill bitmap from the mapping table f->mt for each set bit, clears those bits in the map block and returns the mapping target of the first set bit's entry; with last true it neither touches fill nor clears map and returns the rule index of the block's lowest set bit. The function returns -1 if no block matched (including an empty range). With last true it returns the rule index from the last matching block scanned (each match overwrites the result). With last false it returns, for the first matching block only, the refill result divided by XSAVE_YMM_SIZE (later blocks do not change it); per the function's comment this is the first long-word index to check next. It allocates nothing.
note: Reviewer 15 right: with last false the result is set once, from the first matching block, not the last (nft_set_pipapo_avx2.c:840-845); with last true each matching block overwrites it. Old precondition text dropped.

name: nft_pipapo_avx2_lookup_8b_6
prose: Static function nft_pipapo_avx2_lookup_8b_6(map, fill, f, offset, pkt, first, last), an AVX2 lookup step for one field of an nft pipapo set; the caller must be inside a kernel FPU section with ymm15 zero. It scans each 256-bit block i of the bitmaps from offset up to f->bsize / NFT_PIPAPO_LONGS_PER_M256. For each block it ANDs the six buckets selected by pkt[0] .. pkt[5] (each one of 256 buckets). When first is false and the map block is all zero the block is skipped and left unchanged; if the combined bucket result (ANDed with the map block when first is false) is zero it stores zero into the map block (via ymm15). Otherwise it stores that result into the map block and calls nft_pipapo_avx2_refill on it: with last false that call fills the fill bitmap from the mapping table f->mt for each set bit, clears those bits in the map block and returns the mapping target of the first set bit's entry; with last true it neither touches fill nor clears map and returns the rule index of the block's lowest set bit. The function returns -1 if no block matched (including an empty range). With last true it returns the rule index from the last matching block scanned (each match overwrites the result). With last false it returns, for the first matching block only, the refill result divided by XSAVE_YMM_SIZE (later blocks do not change it); per the function's comment this is the first long-word index to check next. It allocates nothing.
note: Same correction as 8b_4 (nft_set_pipapo_avx2.c:926-931).

name: nft_socket_module_init
prose: Static __init function nft_socket_module_init(void): it returns nft_register_expr(&nft_socket_type), which registers the "socket" nftables expression type and returns 0 on success or a negative errno on failure (in which case the type is not registered). It does nothing else; the matching unregistration is done by the module's exit function.
note: Prose matches nft_socket.c:284-287; dropped the unverified claim that registration holds a module reference through type->owner.

name: nr_state3_machine
prose: Static function nr_state3_machine(sk, skb, frametype), the NET/ROM state 3 (connected) frame handler; nr = skb->data[18] is the acknowledged number, and it returns queued, 0 unless the frame was an NR_INFO variant. NR_CONNREQ: sends an internal NR_CONNACK. NR_DISCREQ: sends NR_DISCACK and calls nr_disconnect(sk, 0). NR_CONNACK|NR_CHOKE_FLAG and NR_DISCACK: nr_disconnect(sk, ECONNRESET). NR_RESET: nr_disconnect(sk, ECONNRESET) only if sysctl_netrom_reset_circuit is set. Any other frame type (including NR_INFOACK combined with NR_MORE_FLAG) is ignored. NR_INFOACK with any combination of NR_NAK_FLAG and NR_CHOKE_FLAG (not NR_MORE_FLAG): with the choke flag it sets NR_COND_PEER_RX_BUSY and starts the T4 timer, else clears it and stops T4; if nr_validate_nr fails it stops there; otherwise with NR_NAK_FLAG it calls nr_frames_acked and nr_send_nak_frame, else nr_frames_acked if the peer is busy or nr_check_iframes_acked if not. NR_INFO with any combination of NAK, CHOKE and MORE flags: does the same choke handling and acknowledgement processing (the validate failure does not stop it), then sets queued = 1 and puts skb at the head of nrom->reseq_queue. If NR_COND_OWN_RX_BUSY is set it stops there. Otherwise it repeats a drain loop while nrom->vr changes: frames whose sequence number equals vr are passed to nr_queue_rx_frame (with this frame's NR_MORE_FLAG), advancing vr modulo NR_MODULUS on success, or on failure setting NR_COND_OWN_RX_BUSY and keeping the frame in a temporary queue; frames inside the receive window are kept in the temporary queue; others are freed; the temporary queue is moved back to reseq_queue. Afterwards, if (vl + window) % NR_MODULUS == vr it calls nr_enquiry_response, else it sets NR_COND_ACK_PENDING and starts T2 unless the flag was already set. The skb is consumed (queued or freed) only on the NR_INFO path.
note: Reviewer 15 right: when NR_COND_OWN_RX_BUSY is set the code breaks out before the loop and the window-full / T2 step (nr_in.c:253-254), and also if it becomes set during the loop the ack step still runs; reviewer 1 right (failure sets OWN_RX_BUSY and keeps the frame, 261-266); reviewer 2 right (INFOACK|MORE not handled). Slice cut the head (function at 172).

name: nci_close_device
prose: Static function nci_close_device(ndev) closing an NFC NCI device; it always returns 0. It first cancels pending requests with nci_req_cancel(ndev, ENODEV), then takes ndev->req_lock. If NCI_UP was already clear (test_and_clear_bit) it flushes cmd_wq, synchronously deletes cmd_timer and data_timer, completes a pending data exchange with -ENODEV if NCI_DATA_EXCHANGE is set (nci_data_exchange_complete), releases req_lock and returns 0, without purging the queues or reducing the flags to NCI_UNREG. Otherwise (NCI_UP was set, now cleared) it purges rx_q and tx_q, flushes tx_wq, purges cmd_q, sets cmd_cnt to 1, sets NCI_INIT, sends a reset request (result ignored), calls ndev->ops->close, clears NCI_INIT, flushes cmd_wq, deletes cmd_timer and data_timer, completes a pending data exchange with -ENODEV if one is set, reduces ndev->flags to only NCI_UNREG, releases req_lock, flushes rx_wq (which may itself take req_lock) and returns 0.
note: Prose matches core.c:554-619; reviewers' points (early return skips purge and flag reduction; the data-exchange completion may clear NCI_DATA_EXCHANGE) are right and already in the packet text.

name: nci_ntf_packet
prose: Function nci_ntf_packet(ndev, skb) dispatching an NCI notification; it returns nothing and frees skb exactly once at its end (kfree_skb). It reads the opcode from the control header and strips the header with skb_pull. For a proprietary GID it calls nci_prop_ntf_packet (logging an error if that returns -ENOTSUPP) and goes to the free. Otherwise it switches on the opcode: for CORE_RESET, CORE_CONN_CREDITS, CORE_GENERIC_ERROR, CORE_INTF_ERROR, RF_DISCOVER, RF_INTF_ACTIVATED, RF_DEACTIVATE and NFCEE_DISCOVER notifications it calls the specific handler, and if that returns non-zero it goes straight to the free; for a zero result, for RF_NFCEE_ACTION_NTF (which has no specific handler) and for an unknown opcode (logged with pr_err) it falls through to nci_core_ntf_packet(ndev, opcode, skb) and then frees skb.
note: Reviewer 15 right: unknown opcodes are logged and still passed to nci_core_ntf_packet (ntf.c:1056-1061); the old text said 'only logged'. Also RF_NFCEE_ACTION and handlers that return 0 are passed there too. Slice cut the head (function at 990).

name: tpacket_snd
prose: Static function tpacket_snd(po, msg) sending frames from a packet socket's TX ring; the slice cut its head (function at af_packet.c:2754). It takes po->pg_vec_lock and releases it on every exit. It returns -EBUSY if the tx ring has no pg_vec; with no destination address it uses the cached device and po->num, otherwise it checks the sockaddr_ll length (-EINVAL), looks the device up by index and, for SOCK_DGRAM, checks the address length (-EINVAL); a missing device gives -ENXIO and a device that is down -ENETDOWN. The device reference taken is dropped before returning (out_put). Control messages are processed with sock_cmsg_send (error returned). It then loops over frames with status TP_STATUS_SEND_REQUEST. With no frame ready, if waiting is allowed and frames are pending it waits (returning -ETIMEDOUT or -ERESTARTSYS on timeout or signal, a negative errno even if frames were already sent) and re-checks; otherwise it leaves the loop and returns the total bytes sent (len_sum). For each frame it parses the header, handles an optional virtio header, stops the loop (returning len_sum) if the byte count would overflow, allocates an skb (on failure it returns len_sum if some bytes were already sent, else the error), fills it (size or format errors give a negative tp_len), and checks the MTU (-EMSGSIZE). On such a frame error: in TP_LOSS mode the frame is marked TP_STATUS_AVAILABLE, the head advances, the skb is freed and the loop continues; otherwise the frame is marked TP_STATUS_WRONG_FORMAT, the skb freed and the negative error returned. It then allocates the zerocopy uarg (len_sum if bytes were sent, else -ENOMEM, on failure), marks the frame TP_STATUS_SENDING, counts it pending and calls packet_xmit; a transmit error is returned (as a negative errno) only if the skb was already destroyed and the frame status is TP_STATUS_AVAILABLE, otherwise it is treated like congestion and the loop continues. Each successfully handed-off frame advances the head and adds its length to len_sum. The return value is therefore len_sum (zero or positive) when the loop ends normally, on integer-overflow stop, or when a later allocation fails after some frames were sent, and a negative errno on the other error paths, even if earlier frames were sent.
note: Reviewer 15 right: after some frames were sent, a wait timeout (-ETIMEDOUT/-ERESTARTSYS, af_packet.c:2841-2846) or a non-loss frame error (2901-2913) returns the negative errno, not the partial count; only the skb-allocation and uarg-allocation failures and the normal loop exit return len_sum (2886-2891, 2924-2931, 2966).

name: packet_set_ring
prose: Static function packet_set_ring(sk, req_u, closing, tx_ring) (re)configuring or removing the RX or TX ring of a packet socket; the slice held only its tail (function at af_packet.c:4546). When not closing it returns -EBUSY if the socket is memory-mapped (po->mapped) or the ring has pending packets. If tp_block_nr is non-zero it requires rb->pg_vec to be NULL (-EBUSY) and validates the request: -EINVAL for a non-positive or non-page-aligned block size, a V3 block too small for its private area plus a minimal frame, a frame size below the minimum or not aligned, zero frames per block, an overflow, or frame_nr different from frames_per_block * block_nr; -ENOMEM if alloc_pg_vec fails; for V3 TX rings it returns -EINVAL if retire timeout, private size or feature word is set; for V1/V2 RX rings it allocates the owner bitmap (-ENOMEM on failure). If tp_block_nr is zero (remove the ring) it returns -EINVAL if tp_frame_nr is non-zero, otherwise no allocation is done. It then detaches the socket from the network (num set to 0, protocol hook unregistered if it was running, synchronize_net) and takes pg_vec_lock. If closing or the socket is not mapped (and, for a non-closing TX ring, nothing is pending) it swaps in the new pg_vec (NULL when removing, which frees the old ring below), owner map, frame_max, head, frame_size, order, length and pages, sets prot_hook.func (tpacket_rcv if an RX ring exists, else packet_rcv) and purges the ring's queue, returning 0; otherwise the result stays -EBUSY and the previous ring is left in place. It then restores po->num and re-registers the hook if it was running and the device binding is still valid (this happens on failure as well), stops the V3 retire timer for a replaced RX ring, and frees whichever pg_vec (and owner map) is left in the local variable (the old ring after a swap, or the new one after a failure).
note: Reviewer 15 right: with tp_block_nr == 0 and tp_frame_nr == 0 the non-closing call also swaps out and frees the old ring and returns 0 (af_packet.c:4645-4651, 4669-4684). The old text said failures leave the previous ring intact and temporaries freed, which holds, but omitted the remove-ring path and the late -EBUSY case when the socket became mapped.

name: qrtr_tx_wait
prose: Static function qrtr_tx_wait(node, dest_node, dest_port, type) deciding whether a data packet must request a confirmation (confirm_rx); it may sleep. It returns 0 at once if type is not QRTR_TYPE_DATA. Otherwise, under qrtr_tx_lock, it finds the tx flow for (dest_node, dest_port) or tries to allocate and insert one; if there is none it returns 1. It then waits interruptibly on the flow's wait queue (under its lock) until flow->pending is below QRTR_TX_FLOW_HIGH, flow->tx_failed is set, or node->ep is NULL. If the wait was interrupted it returns that negative errno; else if node->ep is NULL it returns -EPIPE; else if tx_failed is set it clears it and returns 1 (pending is not incremented); otherwise it increments flow->pending (after the wait, not on the error paths) and returns 1 if pending now equals QRTR_TX_FLOW_LOW, else 0.
note: Reviewer 15 wrong: flow->pending is incremented only in the final else branch, after the wait and not on the interrupted, -EPIPE or tx_failed paths (af_qrtr.c:287-302); the old text was right on this. Rewritten for clarity.

name: rds_rdma_cm_event_handler_cmn
prose: Static function rds_rdma_cm_event_handler_cmn(cm_id, event, isv6), the RDS RDMA connection-manager event handler; it returns 0 when the cm_id is to be kept and non-zero when rdma_cm should destroy it. If cm_id->context holds a connection it takes conn->c_cm_lock and releases it at the exit. If the connection is RDS_CONN_DISCONNECTING it jumps to the exit, returning 1 for RDMA_CM_EVENT_CONNECT_REQUEST (reject) and 0 for other events. By event: CONNECT_REQUEST returns 1 if the device is not an IB channel adapter, else the result of trans->cm_handle_connect. ADDR_RESOLVED (with a connection): drops the connection and returns 0 if the device is not an IB CA; otherwise sets the service type and RNR timer and calls rdma_resolve_route; if that fails it drops the connection and returns 0. ROUTE_RESOLVED (with a connection): if the connection's i_cm_id is this cm_id it sets the service level in the first path record and returns the result of trans->cm_initiate_connect (which can be non-zero), otherwise it drops the connection and returns 0. ESTABLISHED calls trans->cm_connect_complete. REJECTED: drops the connection (and falls back to the compat protocol version when tos is 0) only if there is no reject data or the reject data is at least sizeof(int) long with a value <= RDS_RDMA_REJ_INCOMPAT. ADDR_ERROR, ROUTE_ERROR, CONNECT_ERROR, UNREACHABLE, DEVICE_REMOVAL, ADDR_CHANGE, DISCONNECTED and TIMEWAIT_EXIT drop the connection (when one exists); an unknown event is logged. All of these return 0 apart from the non-zero results noted above.
note: Both reviewer points are right and already in the packet text (cm_initiate_connect result returned on ROUTE_RESOLVED, rds_conn_drop on REJECTED only for small reject codes, rdma_transport.c:137, 153-163). Tightened wording; slice cut the head (function at 49).

name: rds_sendmsg
prose: Function rds_sendmsg(sock, msg, payload_len) sending an RDS message; the caller does not hold the socket lock, and the slice cut the head (function at send.c:1108). Parameter errors: -EOPNOTSUPP for msg_flags other than MSG_DONTWAIT, MSG_CMSG_COMPAT and MSG_ZEROCOPY; for a given destination, -EINVAL for a too-short address, an unsupported family, an IPv4 ANY, broadcast or multicast address (also when mapped in IPv6), a non-unicast non-mapped IPv6 address, or a link-local IPv6 address without scope id; with no destination it takes the connected address under the socket lock. Under the lock it returns -ENOTCONN if the bound or destination address is unspecified, and for an explicit destination -EOPNOTSUPP if one address is IPv4-mapped and the other not, and -EINVAL for conflicting scope ids. Next: the error of rds_rdma_bytes, -EMSGSIZE if the payload or RDMA payload exceeds RDS_MAX_MSG_SIZE or the payload exceeds the send buffer, -EOPNOTSUPP for zerocopy on a non-TCP transport, the error of rds_rm_size, -ENOMEM if the message cannot be allocated, and the errors of rds_message_alloc_sgs and rds_message_copy_from_user. It finds or creates the outgoing connection (error of rds_conn_create_outgoing), selects the path, parses control messages with rds_cmsg_send (error returned), returns -EOPNOTSUPP if an RDMA or atomic op is requested on a transport without support, -EAGAIN if the connection is being destroyed, waits for congestion (error returned), and queues the message; if the send queue is full it returns -EAGAIN when non-blocking, else it waits interruptibly, returning -ETIMEDOUT on timeout or the wait error. After queueing it calls rds_send_xmit; a result of -ENOMEM or -EAGAIN becomes 0 and schedules the send worker unless the connection is being destroyed (then -ENETUNREACH is returned); other results of rds_send_xmit are ignored. On success it drops the message reference, frees the cmsg vector and returns payload_len; any MR allocated on the fly by an RDMA_MAP cmsg is kept. On every failure (out label) it frees the cmsg vector, destroys such an on-the-fly MR (rds_rdma_unuse) and drops the message reference if one was allocated, then returns the error.
note: Prose matches send.c:1108-1419; no reviewer claim beyond the mechanical name one.

name: soft_store
prose: Static sysfs store function soft_store(dev, attr, buf, count) for the rfkill 'soft' attribute. It returns -EPERM if the caller lacks CAP_NET_ADMIN, the error of kstrtoul(buf, 0, &state) if parsing fails, and -EINVAL if the value is greater than 1; none of these touch the rfkill state. Otherwise it takes rfkill_global_mutex, calls rfkill_sync(rfkill) and rfkill_set_block(rfkill, state) (1 blocked, 0 unblocked), releases the mutex and returns count.
note: Matches rfkill/core.c:762-785; slice did not contain the definition (name outside slice).

name: rose_bind
prose: Static function rose_bind(sock, uaddr, addr_len) binding a ROSE socket. Without taking the lock it returns -EINVAL if addr_len is neither sizeof(struct sockaddr_rose) nor sizeof(struct full_sockaddr_rose), srose_family is not AF_ROSE, the short form has more than one digipeater, or srose_ndigis exceeds ROSE_MAX_DIGIS. It then takes lock_sock and releases it before every later return. If the socket does not have SOCK_ZAPPED set it returns -EINVAL (already bound); if no device matches srose_addr it returns -EADDRNOTAVAIL. The source call is taken from the user association for the effective uid when there is one; otherwise, if ax25_uid_policy is set and the caller lacks CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE it drops the device reference and returns -EACCES, else the source call comes from the address. On success it stores the source address, the device (keeping its reference in rose->device) and the digipeaters (from the full form or the single digi of the short form), inserts the socket with rose_insert_socket, clears SOCK_ZAPPED and returns 0.
note: Reviewer right: the SOCK_ZAPPED check is made after lock_sock and returns through out_release (af_rose.c:755-758), so it is not an unlocked early return. Slice cut the head (function at 732).

name: rxrpc_bundle_has_space
prose: Static function rxrpc_bundle_has_space(bundle), which decides whether a client bundle has room for a call and may add a connection; the caller holds the lock protecting the bundle (this function takes none). It clears bundle->alloc_error and counts the connections in bundle->conns that rxrpc_may_reuse_conn accepts (usable), remembering the first slot that is not reusable. If there are none and bundle->upgrade is set it sets bundle->try_upgrade to true. If usable is 0, or if bundle->avail_chans is empty, bundle->try_upgrade is false and usable is less than the number of slots, it tries to add a connection: it returns the result of rxrpc_add_conn_to_bundle(bundle, slot) for the remembered slot, which replaces any old connection in the slot, allocates a new client connection and, on success, marks that slot's channels available and returns true; on allocation failure it stores the error in bundle->alloc_error and returns false. Otherwise it returns usable converted to bool, i.e. true. A slot is always found when usable is less than the number of slots; when every slot is reusable the second test cannot select the allocation path, so the 'no slot' false return in the code is not reachable in practice.
note: Reviewers 1, 2 and 15 right: try_upgrade is set only when bundle->upgrade is set and nothing is usable, and when all slots are reusable the function returns true early (conn_client.c:389-401); the old text's 'false with alloc_error 0 if no non-reusable slot exists' cannot occur.

name: rxrpc_post_challenge
prose: Static function rxrpc_post_challenge(conn, skb) routing a connection-level CHALLENGE packet. It always takes a challenge-input reference on conn and stores it in sp->chall.conn (overwriting whatever was there). If the connection's security has no challenge_to_recvmsg op it posts the packet to the connection's work queue with rxrpc_post_packet_to_conn and returns true. Otherwise, under rcu_read_lock, it looks through the channels for a call with a socket: respond is set when such a call exists, and the loop stops at the first one whose socket has RXRPC_SOCK_MANAGE_RESPONSE. If no call with a socket exists it drops the reference, sets sp->chall.conn to NULL and returns false. If a call with MANAGE_RESPONSE was found it passes the skb to rxrpc_notify_socket_oob; if that does not queue it, it drops the reference, sets sp->chall.conn to NULL and returns false. If no such call was found (calls with sockets exist, but none with MANAGE_RESPONSE) it posts the packet to the connection's work queue. In the true cases the reference stays in sp->chall.conn for later use.
note: Both reviewer points are right and already in the packet text: the function assigns sp->chall.conn itself (conn_event.c:441-442), and returns false when no responding call is found (467-472). Tightened wording.

name: rxrpc_service_connection_reaper
prose: Function rxrpc_service_connection_reaper(work), the work function that reaps service connections (work is rxnet->service_conn_reaper). Under rxnet->conn_lock (write) it scans rxnet->service_conns: it skips connections with a positive active count and those in RXRPC_CONN_SERVICE_PREALLOC. For the rest, if rxnet->live and the connection's local endpoint is not dead, it computes expire_at from idle_timestamp plus rxrpc_connection_expiry * HZ (rxrpc_closed_conn_expiry when the local service is closed); if now is before expire_at it keeps the connection and records the earliest such expiry. A connection that has expired, or any connection when rxnet is not live or the local endpoint is dead, is claimed with atomic_try_cmpxchg of active from 0 to -1 (skipped if that fails), then BUG() if it is a client connection, otherwise unpublished as a service connection and moved to a local graveyard list. After releasing conn_lock it sets the reap timer to the earliest recorded expiry if there was one, then removes each graveyard connection from its list and drops one reference with rxrpc_put_connection (which may start destruction). It returns nothing; conn_lock is not held on return and the graveyard is empty.
note: Prose matches conn_object.c:387-460; the reviewers' points (live/dead handling, unexpired live connections are skipped) are right and already in the packet text.

name: rxrpc_preparse
prose: Static function rxrpc_preparse(prep), the key_type preparse operation for rxrpc keys. If prep->data is NULL and datalen is 0 it accepts a no-security key and returns 0. If datalen is more than 28 bytes it calls rxrpc_preparse_xdr and returns its result unless that is -EPROTO, in which case it tries the version 1 format. For that format it returns -EINVAL if datalen is at most 4 or data is NULL; otherwise it reads and skips the 4-byte version word (advancing prep->data and datalen and zeroing prep->quotalen); -EKEYREJECTED if the version is not 1; -EINVAL if the remaining length is shorter than the v1 structure or does not equal it plus the ticket length; -EPROTONOSUPPORT if the security index is not RXRPC_SECURITY_RXKAD; -EKEYREJECTED if the ticket is longer than AFSTOKEN_RK_TIX_MAX; -ENOMEM if a token or its data cannot be allocated (the allocated token is freed). On success it charges prep->quotalen with the token and data sizes, builds an RXKAD token from the v1 data, increments the token count in prep->payload.data[1], appends the token to the list at prep->payload.data[0], lowers prep->expiry to the token's expiry if that is earlier, and returns 0. (The XDR path likewise appends tokens and charges quotalen inside rxrpc_preparse_xdr_rxkad.)
note: Reviewer 15 wrong: prep->quotalen is updated in this function (key.c:468, set to 0 after the version word, and charged at 516) and in rxrpc_preparse_xdr_rxkad (line 76). The old text was correct on this. Slice cut the head (function at 439).

name: rxperf_init
prose: Static __init function rxperf_init() registering the rxperf server. It allocates the workqueue rxperf_workqueue (-ENOMEM and a log message if that fails), allocates the "rxperf_server" keyring (on failure it logs, keeps -ENOMEM as the result, destroys the workqueue and calls rcu_barrier), and stores the keyring in rxperf_sec_keyring. It adds the rxkad key with rxperf_add_rxkad_key and, with CONFIG_RXGK, calls rxperf_add_yfs_rxgk_key for six enctypes (a negative result from any call fails the init; the helper returns 0 without adding a key when the enctype or key size is unavailable). It then opens the rxrpc socket with rxperf_open_socket. On success it returns 0. If a key addition or the socket opening fails, it puts rxperf_sec_keyring, destroys the workqueue, calls rcu_barrier and returns that negative error (the error from the key helper or the socket open); rxperf_sec_keyring is not reset to NULL.
note: Reviewer 2 right (keyring_alloc failure leaves -ENOMEM as the result, rxperf.c:629, 646-649); reviewer 15 right: rxperf_add_yfs_rxgk_key returns 0 without adding a key when the enctype is unavailable (rxperf.c:594-595), so 'six keys added' was overstated.

name: rxrpc_init_security
prose: Static __init function rxrpc_init_security(void). It walks rxrpc_security_types in order and, for each non-NULL entry, calls its init hook; if one returns a negative value it calls the exit hook of every non-NULL entry with a lower index (not the failing entry's own exit hook), in reverse order, and returns that error. If all init hooks succeed it returns 0. It takes no argument and keeps no lock or reference.
note: Prose matches security.c:28-47. No contract because the function reads a global table (rule 4).

name: tcf_ct_act
prose: Function tcf_ct_act(skb, a, res), the tc ct action; it runs under RCU bottom-half protection and reads the action's params. It updates the action's last-use time and byte statistics first, and uses retval = p->action. With the clear flag it sets post_ct to false, puts and detaches any conntrack entry on the skb and returns p->action, without touching the header. Otherwise it determines the address family (TC_ACT_SHOT after counting a drop if unspecified), pulls the network header and handles fragments: on an error, if the skb is still ours (header checks rejected it) it takes the drop path (TC_ACT_SHOT), else it returns TC_ACT_CONSUMED, counting a drop unless the error is -EINPROGRESS. It then trims the network header (drop on error), reuses cached conntrack state when possible, otherwise looks up the flow table or runs nf_conntrack_in (a verdict other than NF_ACCEPT goes to the verdict handling), applies NAT, may assign a helper and add the seqadj extension (drop on failure), sets mark/labels for commit, runs helpers, confirms the connection on commit, and registers it with the flow table unless skipped. With no conntrack entry on the skb it just pushes the header back. In the success path it pushes the L3 header back, sets tc_skb_cb(skb)->post_ct to true and ->zone to the action zone, sets qdisc_skb_cb pkt_len to skb->len if the packet was defragmented, and returns p->action. Verdict handling for non-accept results: NF_DROP and any unexpected verdict count a drop and return TC_ACT_SHOT (the skb stays with the caller); NF_STOLEN counts a drop and returns TC_ACT_CONSUMED (the skb was taken over and the caller must not touch it).
note: Prose checked against act_ct.c:976-1175; added the defrag-error path where the skb is still ours (drop, TC_ACT_SHOT, 1033-1034) and the no-ct early push. No reviewer claim beyond the mechanical name one.

name: tcf_gate_init
prose: Static function tcf_gate_init(net, nla, est, a, tp, flags, extack) creating or replacing a gate action. It returns -EINVAL if nla is NULL or TCA_GATE_PARMS is absent, the error of nla_parse_nested, and the error of tcf_idr_check_alloc; if the action already exists and bind was requested it returns ACT_P_BOUND (positive) with no parameters installed and no tcf_lock taken. For a new action it calls tcf_idr_create_from_flags (on error tcf_idr_cleanup and the error are returned) and the result will be ACT_P_CREATED; for an existing one without TCA_ACT_FLAGS_REPLACE it releases it with tcf_idr_release and returns -EEXIST. Next it checks the control action (tcf_action_check_ctrlact error), allocates the parameter block (-ENOMEM), parses TCA_GATE_ENTRY_LIST with parse_gate_list (error returned), returns -EINVAL if a new action has no entries ("The entry list is empty"), for a replacement copies the old entries, basetime, clockid, priority and flags as defaults (error of tcf_gate_copy_entries returned), applies the attributes in the request, and resolves the clock with gate_clock_resolve (its error is returned). On any of those failures after the action was created or found, it frees the partly built parameter block and its entries, puts the goto chain if any, and at release_idr sets up the hrtimer with gate_setup_timer if the action was newly created, then calls tcf_idr_release(*a, bind) and returns the error. On success it cancels the timer if needed, then under gact->tcf_lock computes the cycle time if unset, installs the new parameters with rcu_replace_pointer, resets the gate state, sets the control action, starts the timer, and after unlocking puts the previous goto chain and frees the old parameter block through call_rcu; it returns ACT_P_CREATED for a new action or 0 for a replacement.
note: Reviewer 15 wrong: error exits fall through err_free -> chain_put -> release_idr, which calls gate_setup_timer for a newly created action (act_gate.c:538-552), so the old text was right on that. Reviewers 1 and 2 right (ACT_P_BOUND installs nothing; -EINVAL for an empty list on a new action, 433-437). Slice cut the head (function at 347).

name: tcf_ife_encode
prose: Static function tcf_ife_encode(skb, a, res, p) encapsulating a packet in an IFE frame; skb is an Ethernet skb with a valid skb->dev, and p is the action's parameter block with an RCU-protected metalist. It computes metalen with ife_get_sz and the resulting new length, noting whether it would exceed the device MTU (only checked when the skb is not at tc ingress), and always updates the action's byte statistics and last-use time. If metalen is 0 it increments the overlimit statistic and returns the action's verdict without modifying the skb or its Ethernet header. Otherwise, if the configured action is TC_ACT_SHOT or the MTU would be exceeded, it counts a drop and returns TC_ACT_SHOT with the skb unchanged. At ingress it pushes ETH_HLEN, then calls ife_encode(skb, metalen) and each metalist entry's encode callback (accumulating offsets); if ife_encode returns NULL or a callback returns a negative value it counts a drop and returns TC_ACT_SHOT, without undoing the ingress skb_push (the skb has been modified by ife_encode and any callbacks already run). On success it sets the outer Ethernet header's source and destination from p->eth_src and p->eth_dst only when those are non-zero, always sets h_proto to htons(p->eth_type), pulls ETH_HLEN again at ingress, and returns the action's verdict. It takes no lock or reference.
note: Both reviewer points right and already in the packet text: the drop after skb_push at ingress is not undone (act_ife.c:829-848), and the zero-metadata path returns before the header rewrite (814-820). Slice cut the head (function at 787).

name: tc_get_tfilter
prose: Static function tc_get_tfilter(skb, n, extack), the RTM_GETTFILTER handler; the caller does not hold rtnl, and the function takes rtnl_lock only when the qdisc class ops are not QDISC_CLASS_OPS_DOIT_UNLOCKED (or no qdisc was found) or the classifier is not unlocked (rtnl_held), and releases it before returning in that case. It returns the error of nlmsg_parse_deprecated, -ENOENT if the priority is 0, and the error of __tcf_qdisc_find, all as early returns before anything is held. It then returns -EINVAL for a kind name that is too long, and after taking rtnl (if needed) the errors of __tcf_qdisc_cl_find and __tcf_block_find, -EINVAL for a chain index above TC_ACT_EXT_VAL_MASK or a missing chain, and looks up the filter prototype under chain->filter_chain_lock, which is released right after tcf_chain_tp_find: a NULL result gives -ENOENT, an error result is returned, and a kind that differs from the existing filter's gives -EINVAL. With a prototype found it gets the filter handle: a missing handle gives -ENOENT; otherwise it sends an RTM_NEWTFILTER notification with tfilter_notify (a negative result is returned, with an extack message), and then calls tfilter_put on the handle; this tfilter_put runs only on paths that reached the handle lookup. At errout it drops the prototype and chain references if a chain was obtained, releases the block reference (tcf_block_release), unlocks rtnl if it took it, and returns the error (0 when the notification was sent).
note: Reviewer 15 right: tfilter_put is called only after the handle lookup (cls_api.c:2765-2777), not on every return path; the early returns and the goto-errout paths before that skip it. Reviewers 1 and 2 right (the function parses and validates itself; zero priority returns -ENOENT).

name: cake_enqueue
prose: Static function cake_enqueue(skb, sch, to_free) enqueueing a packet into a CAKE qdisc; the slice cut the head (function at sch_cake.c:1738). It classifies the packet with cake_classify; if that returns 0 it counts a drop when the result carries __NET_XMIT_BYPASS, drops the skb to to_free and returns the classification result. Otherwise it refreshes shaper timestamps (possibly scheduling the watchdog), tracks the maximum packet length, and queues the packet: with CAKE_FLAG_SPLIT_GSO and a GSO skb it segments it (on failure it returns qdisc_drop, i.e. NET_XMIT_DROP), queues each segment, adjusts statistics and backlog accounting and consumes the original skb; otherwise it queues the skb, optionally runs the ACK filter, which may remove an earlier ACK from the flow (consuming it and adjusting accounting), and updates statistics. It then updates the overflow heap, the ingress autorate estimate or averaging state, the flow's set membership (sparse, decaying, sparse-wait to bulk) and the maximum buffer usage. If q->buffer_used is within buffer_limit it returns NET_XMIT_SUCCESS. Otherwise it calls cake_drop repeatedly until the buffer is within the limit and records whether any dropped packet came from the same tin and flow as the new packet; it adds the drop count to drop_overlimit and reduces ancestor backlog; if any packet from the same flow was dropped it returns NET_XMIT_CN (after reducing the backlog by one packet less), otherwise NET_XMIT_SUCCESS. On success returns the qdisc owns the skb (or its segments); on classification failure or a segmentation failure the skb is dropped.
note: Reviewer 15 right: NET_XMIT_CN is returned when cake_drop dropped any packet of the same tin and flow (same_flow, sch_cake.c:1933-1947), not only when the just-enqueued packet itself was dropped.

name: pie_process_dequeue
prose: Function pie_process_dequeue(skb, params, vars, backlog) updating PIE's dequeue-side state; it returns nothing and takes no lock. With params->dq_rate_estimator false it sets vars->qdelay to now - pie_get_enqueue_time(skb) if backlog is non-zero, else 0; sets dtime to now - the old vars->dq_tstamp only if that was not DTIME_INVALID (otherwise 0); sets vars->dq_tstamp = now; returns if dtime is 0, and otherwise goes to the burst-allowance step. With the estimator true: if backlog >= QUEUE_THRESHOLD and vars->dq_count == DQCOUNT_INVALID it sets dq_tstamp to the current psched time and dq_count to 0. Then, only if dq_count != DQCOUNT_INVALID, it adds skb->len to dq_count; if the result is >= QUEUE_THRESHOLD it computes dtime = now - dq_tstamp, returns without further change if dtime is 0, else sets avg_dq_rate to (dq_count << PIE_SCALE) / dtime if it was 0, or to avg - (avg >> 3) + (that rate >> 3) otherwise, then sets dq_count to DQCOUNT_INVALID if backlog < QUEUE_THRESHOLD, or to 0 with dq_tstamp refreshed otherwise, and goes to the burst step. In all other cases (dq_count still invalid, or below the threshold) it returns without updating avg_dq_rate, dq_count or burst_time beyond the changes already described. Burst step: if vars->burst_time > 0 it subtracts dtime, clamping to 0 when dtime is at least burst_time.
note: Prose matches sch_pie.c:212-299; reviewers' points (early return when dtime is 0; DQCOUNT_INVALID handling only with the estimator enabled) are right and already in the packet text. Slice cut the head (function at 212).

name: qfq_change_class
prose: Static function qfq_change_class(sch, classid, parentid, tca, arg, extack) creating or changing a QFQ class; *arg is the existing class or 0. It returns -EINVAL if TCA_OPTIONS is missing, and the error of nla_parse_nested_deprecated. The weight is TCA_QFQ_WEIGHT (default 1) rounded through inverse fixed-point arithmetic; lmax is TCA_QFQ_LMAX if given (this function does not range-check an explicit value), otherwise the device MTU, for which it returns -EINVAL if outside [QFQ_MIN_LMAX, QFQ_MAX_LMAX]. For an existing class whose aggregate already has this lmax and weight it returns 0 changing nothing. It returns -EINVAL if q->wsum + delta_w would exceed QFQ_MAX_WSUM. For an existing class, if TCA_RATE is given it replaces the rate estimator (error returned) and goes on to change the aggregate. For a new class it allocates the class (-ENOBUFS on failure), initializes it with the classid, deficit lmax and a default pfifo child qdisc (noop_qdisc if that fails), and creates the estimator if TCA_RATE is given (error returned after destroying the class). Under sch_tree_lock it finds an aggregate for (lmax, weight) or, if none exists, unlocks and allocates one (-ENOBUFS on failure, which kills the class's estimator and destroys a new class; an existing class stays in place), then removes an existing class from its old aggregate or inserts a new one in the class hash, adds the class to the aggregate, unlocks, grows the hash, sets *arg to the class and returns 0.
note: Reviewers 2 and 15 claim a qfq_change_agg path returning -EINVAL for lmax > QFQ_MAX_LMAX; in this version of the code there is no such helper or check for an explicit TCA_QFQ_LMAX (sch_qfq.c:431-441), so the -EINVAL range check applies only to the MTU-derived value; the -ENOBUFS for a failed new-aggregate allocation (511-516) is real and stated. Reviewer 1 right (existing class with equal weight and lmax returns 0 unchanged, 451-452).

name: sfb_enqueue
prose: Static function sfb_enqueue(skb, sch, to_free) of the SFB qdisc. ret starts as NET_XMIT_SUCCESS | __NET_XMIT_BYPASS. If sch->q.qlen is at least q->limit it counts an overlimit and a queue drop and takes the drop exit. It handles the rehash interval (swapping slots or enabling double buffering). With an attached classifier list (read with rcu_dereference_bh) it calls sfb_classify; if that does not give a usable result it goes to other_drop, otherwise the classifier salt provides the hash; without a classifier it uses skb_get_hash_perturb. It updates the per-bucket probabilities for each level, and takes the drop exit (counting a bucket drop) if the minimum bucket length reaches q->max. If the minimum mark probability is at SFB_MAX_PROB (an inelastic flow) it optionally updates the other slot and drops (penalty drop) if sfb_rate_limit says so, else enqueues; otherwise with probability based on p_min it may drop early or ECN-mark the packet with INET_ECN_set_ce (counting a mark; a non-ECN packet is dropped as an early drop). The drop exit calls qdisc_drop_reason on skb and returns NET_XMIT_CN. other_drop counts a qdisc drop if ret has __NET_XMIT_BYPASS, frees skb with kfree_skb and returns ret as set by sfb_classify (NET_XMIT_SUCCESS | __NET_XMIT_STOLEN for stolen, queued or trap results, else the initial bypass value). The enqueue path copies the control block, enqueues into the child qdisc and returns the child's result unchanged: on NET_XMIT_SUCCESS it adds the length to the backlog, increments qlen and the bucket counters; on a drop-counting result it increments the childdrop statistic and the qdisc drop counter.
note: Both reviewer points are right and already in the packet text: other_drop returns ret (possibly NET_XMIT_SUCCESS|__NET_XMIT_STOLEN/BYPASS), not NET_XMIT_CN, and the classifier no-match path frees skb and returns the bypass value (sch_sfb.c:431-435). Slice cut the head (function at 282).

name: sfq_enqueue
prose: Static function sfq_enqueue(skb, sch, to_free) of the SFQ qdisc. It classifies the packet with sfq_classify; on hash 0 it counts a qdisc drop when ret has __NET_XMIT_BYPASS, drops skb to to_free and returns ret. Otherwise it finds the flow slot; with no slot yet it takes a free one (if none is available it returns qdisc_drop(skb, sch, to_free), i.e. NET_XMIT_DROP) and initializes it. For an existing slot with RED configured it computes the average queue and may ECN-mark (counting prob_mark or forced_mark, or marking the head with headdrop) or take the congestion drop path; the drop path also runs when the slot length reaches q->maxdepth. On the congestion drop path without head-drop it returns qdisc_drop (NET_XMIT_DROP); with head-drop it removes the slot's head packet, drops it to to_free, adjusts the backlog by the length difference, queues skb in its place, calls qdisc_tree_reduce_backlog(sch, 0, delta) and returns NET_XMIT_CN. On the normal path it adds skb to the slot, updates backlogs and the flow list, increments sch->q.qlen, and returns NET_XMIT_SUCCESS if qlen is within q->limit. If the limit is exceeded it calls sfq_drop: if the packet dropped came from this slot (its qlen changed) it calls qdisc_tree_reduce_backlog(sch, 0, dropped - qdisc_pkt_len(skb)) and returns NET_XMIT_CN; otherwise it calls qdisc_tree_reduce_backlog(sch, 1, dropped) and returns NET_XMIT_SUCCESS. Packets dropped are transferred to *to_free; on every path where skb was enqueued the qdisc owns it.
note: Both reviewer points right and already in the packet text: NET_XMIT_DROP via qdisc_drop for no free slot or non-headdrop congestion drop (sch_sfq.c:366, 422-423), and the same-flow CN path reduces the backlog by dropped minus skb length (466).

name: taprio_module_init
prose: Static __init function taprio_module_init(): it calls register_netdevice_notifier(&taprio_device_notifier) and returns its error if that fails (nothing is registered then). Otherwise it returns register_qdisc(&taprio_qdisc_ops), 0 on success or a negative errno on failure; on that failure the netdevice notifier stays registered, because the function does no cleanup.
note: Matches sch_taprio.c:2558-2566; reviewer 1 right that the notifier stays registered when register_qdisc fails (already in the packet text).

name: sctp_endpoint_bh_rcv
prose: Static work function sctp_endpoint_bh_rcv(work), processing queued input for an SCTP endpoint (work is ep->base.inqueue.immediate; it may run in BH or task context). It returns nothing. It returns at once if ep->base.dead is set. Otherwise it sets asoc to NULL and pops chunks from the input queue with sctp_inq_pop until it returns NULL, leaving the loop also when sctp_sk(sk)->ep becomes NULL after a dispatch. For each chunk: if first_time is set, the chunk is AUTH and the next chunk header (sctp_inq_peek) is COOKIE-ECHO, it clones chunk->skb into chunk->auth_chunk (GFP_ATOMIC), sets chunk->auth = 1 and continues to the next chunk without dispatching and without clearing first_time; an AUTH first chunk with no following chunk or a different next chunk is processed normally. If chunk->asoc is NULL it looks the association up with sctp_endpoint_lookup_assoc and stores asoc and the transport in the chunk (the local asoc is only refreshed in this case, so it can be NULL or stale when chunk->asoc was already set). The state is asoc->state, or SCTP_STATE_CLOSED when asoc is NULL. If sctp_auth_recv_cid(subtype.chunk, asoc) is true and chunk->auth is not set the chunk is skipped (continue, not dispatched). If asoc is non-NULL and the chunk is DATA it records chunk->transport in asoc->peer.last_data_from; otherwise (any other chunk, or DATA with no asoc) it increments SCTP_MIB_INCTRLCHUNKS and, only if asoc is non-NULL, asoc->stats.ictrlchunks. If chunk->transport is non-NULL it updates its last_time_heard. It then calls sctp_do_sm with the chunk and sets chunk->pdiscard = 1 if that returned non-zero, breaks out if the endpoint was detached, and clears first_time.
note: All three reviewer points are right and the packet text already had them (AUTH skip by continue at endpointola.c:358-362, last_data_from only with asoc, control-chunk MIB counter incremented unconditionally in the non-DATA branch at 398-402).

name: sctp_outq_sack
prose: Function sctp_outq_sack(q, chunk) processing a received SACK against the outqueue (the slice cut its head; function at outqueue.c:1249). It reads the SACK header, adds the gap-ack block count to asoc->stats.gapcnt, and for SFR-CACC, if the primary path has changeover_active, clears it (and cycling_changeover on all transports) when the cumulative ack passes next_tsn_at_change, and resets cacc_saw_newack when gap blocks are present. It advances asoc->highest_sacked, runs sctp_check_transmitted over q->retransmit and over each transport's transmitted list (counting transports that saw a new ack), moves asoc->ctsn_ack_point forward if the cumulative ack is higher, marks missing chunks with sctp_mark_missing when there are gap blocks, and updates unack_data. It then frees chunks on q->sacked whose TSN is at or below the new ctsn_ack_point (decrementing asoc->sent_cnt_removable for a PR-SCTP-capable peer when SCTP_PR_PRIO_ENABLED holds for chunk->sinfo.sinfo_flags, where chunk is the SACK chunk itself), sets asoc->peer.zero_window_announced from the advertised window, sets asoc->peer.rwnd to a_rwnd minus the outstanding bytes (0 if not larger), and calls the stream scheduler's generate_ftsn. It returns sctp_outq_is_empty(q) (1 if the out queue is empty, nothing is outstanding and nothing awaits retransmission, else 0). It takes no lock itself.
note: Prose matches outqueue.c:1249-1410. Noted that the PR-SCTP condition reads chunk->sinfo (the SACK chunk), not the freed chunk (1379-1381). No reviewer claim beyond the mechanical name one.

name: sctp_v4_add_protocol
prose: Static function sctp_v4_add_protocol(): it registers the inetaddr notifier with register_inetaddr_notifier(&sctp_inetaddr_notifier) and returns its error if that fails (nothing registered). Otherwise it registers the IPPROTO_SCTP protocol handler with inet_add_protocol(&sctp_protocol, IPPROTO_SCTP); if that returns a negative value it unregisters the notifier and returns -EAGAIN. If both succeed it returns 0 with the notifier and the handler registered.
note: Matches protocol.c:1298-1314; reviewer 1 right that the notifier-failure path returns its error (already in the packet text).
